Northern Energy Group Names New Chief Operating Officer Amid Growth Plans

Northern Energy Group has appointed industry veteran Lisa Tremblay as its new Chief Operating Officer, the Calgary-based oil and gas producer announced on Thursday. Tremblay, who brings over two decades of experience in upstream operations and project management, will assume her new role effective July 1.

"We are thrilled to welcome Lisa to the executive team," said Northern Energy Group CEO Kevin Muir in a statement. "Her leadership track record and deep operational expertise will be instrumental as we advance our development projects in Western Canada and continue to prioritize safety, efficiency, and sustainable growth."

Tremblay previously served as Senior Vice President of Operations at Canterra Resources, where she oversaw production increases in the Montney and Duvernay plays. In her new position, she will be responsible for overseeing day-to-day operations, optimizing asset performance, and supporting the company’s carbon management initiatives.

Analysts say the appointment comes at a pivotal time for the sector. "With Canadian oil and gas producers facing evolving regulatory requirements and a focus on emissions reduction, operational leadership is more important than ever," said Camila Ng, an analyst at Prairie Research Group.

The Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers welcomed the announcement, noting Tremblay’s reputation for driving operational excellence. "Her appointment is a positive signal for the industry’s ongoing commitment to responsible resource development," said CAPP spokesperson Raj Singh.

Northern Energy Group employs approximately 1,200 staff and produces around 85,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day from assets across Alberta and British Columbia.
